solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fix stamp on and he delivers

indicators.note: to fix something can mean to rework or rearrange it, so the letters of these words are reordered

explanation.surface: A tip for whoever brings the letters: put a stamp on it and it will arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fix' reads as an instruction to attach the stamp, but it signals rearranging the seven letters of STAMP ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A postman is the man whose job is bringing mail to houses.

clue.text: Backstory is Queen in Peru furious with the Spanish

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step
furious suggests the letters are thrown into wild disorder

parts.note: Q is the abbreviation for Queen, as in chess notation
el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: A tale of a queen raging in Peru alongside the Spaniards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'furious' rearranges PERU as PREU, and Q sits inside it ('in' places Q).
explanation.definitionFit: A prequel is a story set before an existing one, telling what came earlier.

clue.text: Learn to reduce jabber in card game?

indicators.note: reducing the word for learn means trimming its final letter

parts.note: to study is to learn
a poker is something that jabs, a jabber

explanation.surface: Advice to talk less while playing cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jabber' looks like chatter but means one who jabs, a poker; the question mark flags that pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Stud poker is a poker variant in which some cards are dealt face up.

clue.text: Gauge to measure temperature rising inside

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the letters read upwards, backwards
inside means the letters are tucked away within the run of clue words

explanation.surface: Instructions for using a gauge to check how hot something is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' finds RETEM in measuRE TEMperature; 'rising' reads it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A meter is an instrument that gauges a quantity, such as a gas or electricity meter.

clue.text: Hang on! Over 100's very quick

indicators.note: over signals that the word for a hundred is turned over and read backwards

parts.note: a ton is 100, especially miles per hour
so means very
fast means quick

explanation.surface: Someone driving at over a hundred is going very fast indeed.
explanation.definitionFit: Not so fast is an exclamation telling someone to wait and not be hasty.

clue.text: Everything in programme's lacking depth

indicators.note: the word for everything sits within the word for a programme

parts.note: a show is a programme on stage or TV
all means everything

explanation.surface: A critic complains that a whole TV programme is superficial.
explanation.definitionFit: Water or thinking that is shallow has little depth, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Almost certain last of group's in time for jet

indicators.note: the picked letter sits within the shortened word
almost means the word stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: sure means certain

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Something nearly sure: the final member of a group arrives in time for the plane.
explanation.walkthrough: SUR (SURE less a letter) takes in P to make SPUR, then T follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A spurt is a sudden jet of liquid gushing out.

clue.text: Perhaps Michael's a moderate between two sides

indicators.note: between places the word for moderate in the middle of the two side letters

parts.note: R and L are right and left, the two sides
to moderate something is to change or alter it

explanation.surface: A politician called Michael is a centrist sitting between the two parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Michael is one of the archangels, so he is an example of the answer.

clue.text: Landowner set's repressing resistance

indicators.note: repressing means holding something down within, so the outer word contains the letter

parts.note: laid means set, as a table is laid
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A landowner's set is crushing opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: A laird is a Scottish landowner of an estate.

clue.text: Succeed in part by charming

parts.note: to win is to succeed
some, as in 'some' of it, means in part

explanation.surface: Getting ahead partly by sheer charm.
explanation.definitionFit: Winsome describes someone attractive in an engaging, appealing way.

clue.text: Delight in lute playing to eat by

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take in, or eat, the multiplication sign
playing suggests the letters of the instrument are being worked around into a new order

parts.note: X is the times sign, as in 3 by 4

explanation.surface: Someone takes joy in strumming a lute while dining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges LUTE as EULT; 'to eat' puts X inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To exult in something is to rejoice in it triumphantly.

clue.text: Finally get judge's agreement — court to stop road intersection

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word that follows

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for judge

indicators.note: the court abbreviation plugs a gap inside the word for agreement, stopping it up

parts.note: a union is an agreement or alliance

explanation.surface: A legal saga: a judge finally rules and the court halts work at a crossroads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to stop' means the court abbreviation plugs the word for agreement; the road sense of 'stop' is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: A T-junction is a place where one road meets another at right angles, shaped like the letter.

clue.text: Prompts EU action at the highest level

indicators.note: action here means the letters are set in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: A demand for the European Union to act at the very top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'action' rearranges the nine letters of PROMPTS EU.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppermost describes something at the top, the very highest position.

clue.text: Notice odd parts of dot-com on increase

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement

indicators.note: odd parts means taking the first, third and fifth letters of the following word

explanation.surface: An advert about a dot-com firm on the up.
explanation.definitionFit: To add to something is to augment it, making it larger.

clue.text: Enjoyed Conservative leaving beaten

indicators.note: leaving means the letter for Conservative departs from the word for beaten

parts.note: licked means beaten, as in thrashed

explanation.surface: An election-night story: a voter loved seeing the Conservative candidate trounced.
explanation.definitionFit: Liked is a past-tense synonym of found pleasure in.

clue.text: Late stage to get completely even

parts.note: the late person is a dead one
a level is a stage, as in a game

explanation.surface: Reaching the final phase to make things perfectly balanced.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead level means perfectly flat or equal, with 'dead' as an intensifier.

clue.text: Recall artist repaired organ that's church's pride

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the artist abbreviation runs backwards

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: repaired suggests the letters are fixed into a new order

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church proudly brings back an artist to restore its organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recall' turns RA into AR; 'repaired' rearranges ORGAN as ROGAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrogance is overbearing pride, an inflated sense of one's own worth.

clue.text: Worker tucked into pan fried topside for Sunday dinner

indicators.note: tucked into means the worker is placed inside the other letters

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly, to roast

indicators.note: in a down clue the top side of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a bee is a worker, as in worker bee

explanation.surface: A cook prepares fried topside of beef for the Sunday meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topside' looks like the cut of beef, but means the first letter of 'fried'. Roast beef is the traditional British Sunday lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Roast beef is the classic British meal served on a Sunday.

clue.text: Present rosier version, it's not a problem

parts.note: now is the present time

indicators.note: a version is a variant form, so these letters appear in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Putting a rosier spin on things to reassure everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' reads as a gift but means the current moment; 'version' signals that ROSIER becomes ORRIES.
explanation.definitionFit: No worries is a casual reassurance meaning there is no trouble at all.

clue.text: Drink ale the bar brewed

indicators.note: brewing mixes ingredients, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone at the pub makes ale on the premises.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbal tea is an infusion of herbs, a hot beverage.

clue.text: Difficult catching a horse that's stressed

indicators.note: catching means the outer word catches and holds the others inside it

parts.note: hard means difficult
gee-gee, GG, is a childish word for a horse

explanation.surface: A tough job catching a nervous horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Haggard describes a face looking exhausted and worn from strain.

clue.text: Grassed areas have new rules to comprehend

indicators.note: comprehend in its old sense of include or contain, so the word for rules holds the letter

parts.note: laws are rules

explanation.surface: Park lawns get a fresh set of regulations that people must understand.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawns are areas of mown grass around houses and parks.

clue.text: Makes sure you're pronounced fit

indicators.note: pronounced means the words are said aloud and heard as another word

parts.note: to see to something is to make sure of it, so this is said as 'sees your'

explanation.surface: A doctor makes certain you are declared healthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit' reads as healthy but is the noun, a convulsion.
explanation.definitionFit: A seizure is a sudden attack or convulsion, which is one sense of the noun fit.

clue.text: Barbecue half of grub poorly

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word gives its first two letters

parts.note: poorly means ill

explanation.surface: A cookout where half the food has gone bad.
explanation.definitionFit: To grill or barbecue is to cook over direct heat, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Keys found in gaps between seats when heading off

indicators.note: heading off means the word loses its first letter, its head

parts.note: aisles are the gaps between rows of seats

explanation.surface: Someone finds their keys between the seats as they leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keys' looks like the door kind but means low islands, as in the Florida Keys.
explanation.definitionFit: Keys are small low islands or reefs, so they are isles.

clue.text: Tip liquid in basin drain regularly, it gives a nice smell

parts.note: a pot is a basin or bowl
to pour is to tip liquid out

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the following word, here the second and fourth

explanation.surface: Kitchen instructions: tip some liquid into a basin and drain it at intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: Potpourri is a bowl of dried petals and spices kept to scent a room.

clue.text: Exercise over a kilometre and you start being sick

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercise
K is short for kilometre

indicators.note: start takes the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Running over a kilometre leaves you feeling unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Peaky is British slang for pale and unwell.

clue.text: Different characters appear during psychotherapy

indicators.note: these letters, the characters, show up within the word that follows

explanation.surface: Odd personalities emerge during therapy sessions.
explanation.definitionFit: Other means different, as in some other way.

clue.text: Ease brief passage through the borders

indicators.note: brief means the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: an alley is a narrow passage
via means through

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone eases themselves through a short passageway along the frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: To alleviate pain is to lessen or relieve it, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Endlessly laud revolutionary country in poem

indicators.note: endlessly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to hail is to praise or laud

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the country abbreviation reads backwards

parts.note: UK is the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: A verse that praises a revolutionary nation without end.
explanation.definitionFit: A haiku is a Japanese form of verse of three short lines.

clue.text: 500 images initially spread out for exhibition

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the following word

parts.note: to splay is to spread out

explanation.surface: Five hundred pictures laid out for a gallery show.
explanation.definitionFit: A display is a show or exhibition of items for people to view.

clue.text: Expect payment to protect mineral deposits

indicators.note: the word for payment wraps around and shields the mineral deposits

parts.note: a fee is a payment
ores are deposits of metal-bearing minerals

explanation.surface: A mining firm anticipates paying to safeguard its seams.
explanation.definitionFit: To foresee is to predict, to anticipate what will happen.
